newsitem.title: USA: N.Carolina challenges FDA on tobacco regulations.
newsitem.headline: N.Carolina challenges FDA on tobacco regulations.

text.p: The state of North Carolina filed a brief in federal district court on Tuesday challenging the Federal government's authority to regulate tobacco products as a drug.
The amicus curiae brief joins a lawsuit by major tobacco manufacturers against efforts to classify tobacco as a drug.
N.C. Attorney General Mike Easley filed the brief in U.S. District Court in Greensboro, charging the U.S. Food and Drug Administration was wrong to take on Congress' role.
He said Congress has always been responsible for placing health and advertising restrictions on tobacco products and for exercising authority over tobacco itself.
"...the FDA crossed the line from implementing congressional policy and executing laws enacted by Congress to fashioning the law that it believes the law should be," Easley wrote in the brief.

The brief calls on the court to find the tobacco rules unconstitutional and block the FDA from enforcing them. The filing comes in the final stretch of the campaign season for N.C. Governor Jim Hunt who is seeking re-election, as well as contenders for the U.S. House of Representatives and Senate.
Tobacco has become a hot-button issue on the stump in North Carolina since the state leads the nation in tobacco production. Its sales topped $1 billion last year.
In August, President Bill Clinton authorized the FDA to regulate the sale and marketing of cigarettes in an effort to curb smoking among children.

"This regulatory power grab is even more astonishing in light of the fact that the FDA has previously admitted in federal court that it has not such lawful authority," the brief read. Easley said to claim tobacco products are drugs sends the wrong message to states.
